title: Vodafone Idea Posts ₹52,000-Crore Profit — But Strip Away the Accounting Magic, and the Survival Fight Continues
excerpt: India's third-largest telecom operator reports its first profit in six years, powered almost entirely by a government AGR reprieve — yet NRI investors face the same old question: can Vi survive the Jio-Airtel duopoly?
body:
The headline number is staggering: Vodafone Idea reported a consolidated net profit of ₹51,970 crore for the quarter ended March 31, 2026 — its first in roughly six years, and a swing from a loss of ₹7,167 crore in the same period a year ago. But before NRI investors break out the champagne, a closer look at the fine print reveals that the profit is almost entirely the product of an accounting adjustment rather than a business turnaround.

## The AGR Reprieve

The story begins on April 30, when the Department of Telecom informed Vodafone Idea that a reassessment committee had finalised the company's adjusted gross revenue (AGR) dues at ₹64,046 crore for the period FY 2006-07 to FY 2018-19 — a reduction of approximately 27% from the earlier assessment of ₹87,695 crore.

Under Indian accounting standards (Ind AS 109), Vi derecognised the old financial liability of ₹80,502 crore and recognised the revised figure of ₹24,880 crore, releasing a one-time exceptional gain of ₹55,622 crore through the profit and loss statement. Additionally, the Centre granted a five-year moratorium on these payments. Strip away that exceptional item, and Vi's operating loss for the quarter was approximately ₹5,515 crore — a figure that tells a rather different story.

## The Operating Reality

Revenue from operations grew a modest 3% year-on-year to ₹11,332 crore — the lowest growth rate among India's three private telecom operators. The average revenue per user (ARPU) rose to ₹190, the highest year-on-year growth in the industry at 8.3%, but still the lowest absolute ARPU among private operators.

The subscriber base stood at 19.28 crore, and Vi noted that monthly subscriber additions had been trending upward since February — a small but significant inflection after years of customer haemorrhage to Reliance Jio and Bharti Airtel.

Capital expenditure hit ₹2,294 crore for the quarter and ₹8,742 crore for the full year, as the company expanded its 5G network to 83 cities. But it remains vastly outspent by Jio and Airtel, both of which have deployed 5G across hundreds of cities.

For the full fiscal year 2026, Vi posted an annual profit of ₹34,552 crore (versus a ₹27,384-crore loss in FY25), with revenue of ₹44,782 crore.

## The Capital Lifeline

Alongside the results, Vi announced a ₹4,730-crore fundraising plan. The board approved the issuance of up to 430 crore warrants — each convertible into one equity share at ₹11 per warrant — to Suryaja Investments, a Singapore-based Aditya Birla Group entity and promoter company.

The timing is deliberate. Kumar Mangalam Birla recently returned as Vi's non-executive chairman for the second time, signalling that the promoter group remains committed to the company's survival. The capital infusion provides some runway for network investment and debt servicing, though Vi's total deferred payment obligations still stood at a formidable ₹1,52,614 crore (₹1,27,360 crore for spectrum and ₹25,254 crore for AGR) as of March 31.

## What Brokerages Are Saying

The market's verdict was mixed. Vi's stock has surged 79.25% year-to-date, pricing in the AGR relief well before it hit the profit-and-loss statement. But on the day after results were announced, shares fell over 2%.

Macquarie and UBS acknowledged the operational stabilisation but maintained cautious outlooks, citing the debt-to-equity ratio of 13.5 times and a negative book value of ₹-15.03 per share. Citi noted "better funding visibility" but emphasised that Vi's viability still depends on further tariff increases across the industry and continued government support.

## The Diaspora Angle

Among NRI retail investors, Vi remains one of the most polarising stocks on the Indian bourses. Online forums from Reddit's r/IndiaInvestments to WhatsApp NRI trading groups have debated the turnaround thesis for years. The AGR relief and Birla's return give the bulls fresh ammunition. But the bears point to a fundamental question: can a telecom operator with the lowest ARPU, the smallest 5G footprint, and the highest debt survive in a market dominated by two well-capitalised giants?

## What's Next

Vi's ₹7,076 crore in deferred-payment instalments due by March 2027 will be the next test of its cash-flow resilience. The company needs sustained ARPU growth, a credible 5G rollout, and — crucially — a third round of industry-wide tariff hikes to close the revenue gap with Jio and Airtel. The accounting profit buys time and sentiment. Whether it buys survival remains an open question.

nri_angle: Vodafone Idea is one of the most watched — and most debated — stocks among NRI retail investors. The stock's 79% year-to-date surge has drawn in diaspora money, but the gap between the headline profit and the underlying operating loss makes this a classic value trap or turnaround bet depending on whom you ask.
